findings.summary: In the new DATA_START state the leading line break is only stripped if a boundary is already buffered; with chunked input and no boundary, nothing is deleted and the state moves to DATA, so streamed contents get a spurious \r\n prefix.

The decoder can emit Data(b'', more_data=True) from DATA_START with chunked input, and the encoder moves to DATA without writing \r\n, so the next non-empty Data follows the headers without a blank line, producing a malformed body.

After a Field or File event the encoder state is now DATA_START, but the set of states allowing a new part doesn't include it, so consecutive Field/File events without Data in between now raise, a regression.
The new test_empty_field only covers the whole message in one buffer and does not exercise the chunked path behind findings 1 and 2.
